page: Microsoft Azure E32pds_v6 is an Epdsv6-family virtual machine powered by an ARM64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores utilizing the Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz, with one thread per core. The memory configuration includes 256.0 GB of RAM, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 1890 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results show strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression all scoring in the top 25%. Memory performance is a key strength, with large-block read-only and write memory bandwidth, Passmark memory score, and Passmark database operations all ranking in the top 10% tier. However, single-core performance remains in the average tier across stress-ng, Geekbench, and bzip3 tests.

While the server demonstrates strong capabilities in database operations and static web serving, it exhibits limitations in heavy computational tasks. Specifically, LLM inference prompt processing for large 70B models falls into the bottom 10% tier, though text generation for the same model size remains average. Given the high memory-to-core ratio and top-tier database benchmark results, this server is suited for memory-intensive workloads, database management, software compilation, and web serving, offering qualitative resource density and memory efficiency for ARM-native deployments.
